newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Toatsu Vietnam JV to build production plant.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Toatsu Vietnam JV to build production plant.

text.p: Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc said on Wednesday that its joint venture in Vietnam would spend $50 million to build a production facility for vinyl chloride resin.
The new facility, expected to start operating in April 1998, will have a production capacity of 80,000 tonnes per year, the company said in a statement.

The joint venture, Mitsui Vina Plastic and Chemical Corp, is 36 percent owned by Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals, 24 percent owned by Thai Plastic & Chemicals Public Co Ltd of Thailand and 10 percent owned by Mitsui & Co Ltd.
The state-run Vietnam National Chemical Corp and Vietnam Plastic Corp also own 15 percent each in the joint venture.
The site acquired for the new facility is located about 70 km southeast of Ho Chi Minh City, the statement said.
The new factory would be the first production facility for vinyl chloride resin in Vietnam, a Mitsui Toatsu spokesman said.
Vinyl chloride resin is used mainly for plastic water pipes.
